activities.name: Manali–Leh highway and the Ladakh passes
activities.note: crosses the Baralacha La, Lachulung La and Tanglang La passes, which close under snow from November to May

windows.reason: shut under snow. The highway opens to civilian traffic in late May — 27 May in 2025, 19 May in 2024 — and closes between late October and mid-November (20 November in 2025)
the opening and closing months; the date differs from year to year
the season is ending, and some high passes begin closing under early snow
the sweet spot of the season, with the high passes open through mid-September

activities.name: Ladakh in the monsoon
activities.note: Ladakh sits in the Himalayan rain shadow, so the monsoon that soaks the rest of northern India mostly misses it

windows.reason: dry and open on the plateau while the plains are under monsoon — though landslides on the approach passes, south of the range, can still close the road

activities.name: Tiger safaris in Ranthambore
activities.note: the core zones are the ones for tigers; some buffer zones may still run safaris in the monsoon, depending on rain and forest department rules

windows.reason: the core zones close for the monsoon, from July to September, and reopen in October
water sources dry up, tigers gather at the lakes and waterholes, and thin cover makes them easier to spot

activities.name: Kanha, Bandhavgarh and Pench tiger reserves
activities.note: the buffer zones stay open for safaris while the cores are shut

windows.reason: the core zones close for the monsoon breeding season and road repairs, reopening on 1 October

activities.name: Dhikala zone, Corbett National Park
activities.note: Dhikala is Corbett's best-known zone; the Jhirna and Dhela zones stay open all year, weather permitting

windows.reason: shut for the monsoon, for visitor safety
open only until 15 June, when the zone closes for the monsoon
the zone reopens on 15 November, so only the second half of the month is bookable

activities.name: Valley of Flowers trek
activities.note: the national park is open only from 1 June to 31 October

windows.reason: peak bloom, from mid-July to mid-August, when the monsoon brings the valley into full flower
the park is open but the flowering is either still to come or fading

activities.name: Kedarnath temple pilgrimage
activities.note: the temple is snowbound and shut for about six months each winter, while worship moves to Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath

windows.reason: the pilgrimage season, between the spring reopening and the winter closing
the doors reopen in spring on a date announced each year and timed by the ascendant — 22 April in 2026
the doors close for winter on Bhai Dooj, which falls in late October or November — 3 November in 2024, 23 October in 2025

activities.name: Skiing at Gulmarg
activities.note: the ski season runs from about late December to late March

windows.reason: the most reliable snow, from the second half of January through February
the edges of the season: snow cover is building in December, and March snow can change fast in warmer days

activities.name: Pushkar Camel Fair
activities.note: the fair follows the Hindu lunar calendar, so its dates move each year

windows.reason: held in the month of Kartik and ending on its full moon, usually late October or November, with camel trading, races and folk music

activities.name: Diving off Havelock (Swaraj Dweep)
activities.note: the dive season runs from October to May

windows.reason: the peak: the steadiest seas, mild currents and the most marine life, though also the busiest weeks
the southwest monsoon brings strong winds and rough seas; boat trips are cancelled at short notice and only a few centres dive
